title: feat: Use margin-bottom/gap spacing in more places
description:
Fixes #672

* For consistency, I renamed `.bslib-mb-spacer` to `.bslib-mb-spacing`. I'm hoping this helps when trying to remember the class/variable names. The reasoning is that `--bslib-spacer` (the custom CSS property) is non-commital since it hasn't been applied anywhere. `--bslib-mb-spacer` is a similar unit. But once it's a class, we use `-spacing`, i.e. `.bslib-gap-spacing` and `.bslib-mb-spacing`, which I read as "the elements in this container use _gap spacing_ or this element uses _margin bottom spacing_". Obviously, it's not perfect.

    * Alternative: we could use `.bslib-mb` or `.mb-bslib` instead, since there is a difference that this class directly sets the margin bottom of the current element.

* While here I added something that feels relevant: setting `margin-bottom: 0` on fill items with bslib's margin bottom spacing that are activated within a fillable container.

* `layout_columns()` and `layout_column_wrap()` gain the `.bslib-mb-spacing` class so that they naturally have some bottom margin in a flow context. This also motivated adding the above consideration for `.bslib-mb-spacing` fill items.

* `sidebar()` gains `gap` and `padding` arguments to control the gap and padding within the sidebar itself. `gap` picks up from `--bslib-spacer` or the inline style, and I added a CSS variables `--bslib-sidebar-content-padding` because `--bslib-sidebar-padding` needs to be a single value and is used in a few places that aren't specifically a `padding` property. The `.sidebar-content` container also gains the `.bslib-gap-spacing` so that bottom margin is dropped in sidebars in favor of the `gap` spacing.

title: docs: Reorganize articles
description:
This biggish PR brings a bit more organization to our articles. The key idea is that I've moved articles into their own directories where their files can be self-contained. Here's a quick summary of this PR:

1. Articles now live in their own directory, with all their supporting files. E.g. `vignettes/cards.Rmd` is now `vignettes/cards/index.Rmd`.

2. Supporting files, such as images and examples, are stored alongside the article, e.g. `vignettes/cards/shiny-hex.svg`. Shared files _could_ be stored in `vignettes/` but we don't have any at the moment.

3. Rendered iframe and images are now stored in `examples/` folders within the article source folder. I've also added checks to enforce that these example chunks are named. Without this check, it's easy to end up with link churn, e.g. `unnamed-chunk-4` becomes `unnamed-chunk-6` after minor editing.

4. I added pkgdown redirects from the old article locations to the new locations.

5. I used a local link-checker (code below) to make sure I hadn't missed any internal reference changes.

<details><summary>Link Checking</summary>

```r
library(tidyverse)
library(jsonlite)

pkgdown::clean_site()
pkgdown::build_site()

# In background terminal
# cd docs/
# # npm install -g http-server
# http-server

processx::run(
  command = "muffet",
  args = c(
    "http://127.0.0.1:8080/articles/index.html", 
    "--json"
  ),
  stdout = "linkcheck.json",
  error_on_status = FALSE
)

x <- fromJSON("./linkcheck.json", simplifyDataFrame = FALSE)

x |>
 map_dfr(~ .) |>
 rename(source = url) |>
 unnest_wider(links) |> 
 filter(
  !str_detect(error, "^dial"),    # connection errors
  !str_detect(url, "blob/HEAD/"), # Links to GitHub source files
  !str_detect(url, "bs[45]-variables/?(index.html)?#") # false negative
)
```

</details>

title: fix(card): Update full-screen focus trap logic
description:
Changes from #662 have affected the visibility and tab focus order of the full screen enter button. This PR updates the focus trap logic in two ways:

* Because the full screen enter button retains focus when entering full screen mode, we now detect this case and move focus to the parent card when making the card full screen. We also do this step a little later (after adjusting the full screen attribute and setting classes on the document body).

* The full screen enter button is included in the list of focusable elements, even when the card is in full screen. Helpfully, it's always the last element. We remove it from our list of focusable elements so that we skip it when the user reaches the end of the card.

This issue was uncovered by [313-bslib-card-tab-focus](https://rstudio.github.io/shinycoreci/results/2023/07/19/#313-bslib-card-tab-focus).

title: Attach component-specific Sass/Css at the component level; allow for more customization via CSS variables
description:
Currently, `bs_theme()` imports Sass files for bslib components (e.g., cards, sidebars, etc), which has a couple benefits:

1. Allows us to leverage Sass features like `@extend` and placeholders that, in effect, modify Bootstrap.
2. Minimizes `sass::sass()` calls (since sass may need to be re-compiled for each component).
3. Reduces complexity in the `HTMLDependency()` of these components. 

However, there are downsides that outweigh those benefits:

1. Components currently don't work in Quarto (https://github.com/quarto-dev/quarto-cli/issues/6081). This is because Quarto brings it's own Bootstrap dependency. It actually does this by copying over bslib's patched version of Bootstrap, so it could, in theory, also bring over the component Sass, but it feels wrong to increase the potential for issues brought about by incompatibility between build-time vs run-time dependencies.
2. Generally it's a bit weird and confusing to bundle these components with the core Bootstrap bundle.
4. We're shipping more CSS than needed for some apps (this will continue to get worse as we build out more components)

This PR moves component-level Sass out of `bs_theme()` and into the relevant components. And since do might need to re-compile Sass in those situations, it follows the [dynamically theme-able component model](https://rstudio.github.io/bslib/articles/custom-components.html#dynamically-themeable-component). 

Also, while we're here, I took the opportunity to reduce the amount of Sass specific calculations (by moving what we can to CSS), and more fully embrace CSS variables for customization. We'll still keep Sass around to leverage things like `mix()` and `color-contrast()`, but once CSS has good support for these things, we could potentially remove the (run-time) Sass dependency for these components, and still allow them to be theme-able (by allowing defaults to derive from Bootstrap's CSS variables)

description:
This PR improves our use of S3 classes around preset themes:

1. `bs_preset_bundle()` takes a preset object but doesn't use S3 for dispatching. If it's not a `preset` or if `preset$type` is missing, the bundle returns `NULL`.

2. `bs_theme()`, when a preset is added to the theme, returns an object with class `bs_theme_with_preset`, in addition to a version-specific class. To determine the preset name and type, call `theme_preset_info()` to read the values from the sass bundle.

3. The preset bundles now include two SASS variables, `$bslib-preset-name` and `$bslib-prest-type`, that encode the name and type of the preset. We already included `$bootstrap-version`, so it's now possible to completely extract the theme information from the SASS bundles. I added `theme_preset_info()` that does just this. 

    * Extracting variables from the SASS layers is slow enough that I think it's worth testing for the presence of `bs_version_N` or `bs_theme_with_preset` classes before making the more expensive call to `bs_get_variables()`.
    * The SASS variables are now defined in `bs_theme_init()` so they're guaranteed to exist for all `bs_theme()`-created themes. I've also added rules that create CSS variables, e.g. `--bslib-bootstrap-version` and `--bslib-prest-name` etc, to allow us to know the Bootstrap version and our preset values even in the compiled CSS.

title: feat!(bs_theme): Rename `preset` from `name`
description:
In #629, we added a new `name` argument to replace the `bootswatch` argument. Eventually, in that PR, I settled into a "preset" as the name for a "starter theme", i.e. a _preset_ covers Bootswatch themes and themes provided by bslib.

This PR renames `name` in `bs_theme()` to `preset`, which is more descriptive and has clearer intent, especially when we start using the word _preset_ more often in our documentation.

title: Add fonts for new builtin Shiny theme preset
description:
Closes #630 and adds the desired font stack for the new Shiny theme, namely Open Sans and Source Code Pro.

This PR updates the `tools/download_bootswatch_fonts.R` script to also download fonts for builtin presets. This necessitated a few changes:

1. `tools/download_bootswatch_fonts.R` is now `tools/download_preset_fonts.R`
2. The download fonts script now looks for `_bootswatch.scss` or `_rules.scss` files (in that order)
3. Builtin presets now must follow this convention:
    * Preset files are stored in `inst/bs{version}/{name}/`
    * Preset scss files should be named according to their layer, e.g. `_variables.scss` and `_rules.scss`.

From what I can tell, these new fonts add ~600KB to the package bundle. We may want to cut back on font weights or figure out how to reduce the package bundle size, but I'm also okay waiting for on that for another PR.

title: New theme preset infrastructure and new "shiny" preset
description:
Closes #627 

## Description

This PR adds internal infrastructure for the concept of a "theme preset", which is either a Bootswatch theme or a built-in theme. It's a _preset_ in the sense that these are settings that are overlaid on a baseline Bootstrap theme, but the theme can be further customized by users using the normal `bs_theme()` infrastructure.

The goal of this work is to introduce a new built-in `"shiny"` theme, while also leaving the door open to future variants, e.g. `"shiny-light"` and `"shiny-dark"`, or to variants specific to Bootstrap version, i.e. `"shiny"` for BS5, `"shiny"` for BS6, etc. The built-in themes work in a similar way to the Bootstrap themes, but they're stored in `inst/custom-themes/bsX/...`.

Part of this change is to supersede the `bootswatch` argument with a new catch-all `name` argument. We retain `bootswatch` for backwards compatibility and enforce that only one of `name` or `bootswatch` is provided:

```r
bs_theme(version = 5, name = "darkly")
#> ...returns the darkly bootswatch theme bundle

bs_theme(version = 5, bootswatch = "darkly")
#> ...is equivalent

bs_theme(version = 5, "darkly")
#> ...as is this

bs_theme(version = 5, "darkly", bootswatch = "darkly")
#> ...throws an error and recommends using `name`
```

The disambiguation between `name` and `bootswatch` is handled via `new_theme_preset()` which takes `name`, `bootswatch` and `version` and returns a `bs_preset` object containing the resolved details of the preset theme. If we resolve the preset to a built-in or bootswatch theme, this preset object is sub-classed `bs_preset_builtin` or `bs_preset_bootswatch`.

This preset object is in turn passed to `bs_preset_bundle()` which dispatches to the correct bundle-providing function. I initially used S3 classes for this but it felt like too much – in particular, I didn't like that `bootswatch_bundle()` (or the S3 method equivalent) would have to take `preset` rather than `bootswatch` and `version`.

`bs_theme_update()` also takes both `name` and `bootswatch` and uses the same `new_theme_preset()` code path to disambiguate. If a new preset is provided, we remove the existing preset – i.e. either the `builtin` or `bootswatch` SASS bundle – and remove the signaling class from the `theme` object – e.g. the class like `bs_bootswatch_darkly` or `bs_builtin_shiny`. We then apply the new theme preset on top. We also retain special behavior for `name = "default"` or `name = "bootstrap"`, in which case `bs_theme_update()` will remove any preset theme bundles from the input `theme`.

## TODO

- This PR doesn't include fonts, which need to be handled via a sass file so that they can be included in the sass bundle. I'll have to investigate how this happens for Bootswatch.

- In this PR, users need to opt into the new shiny theme with `bs_theme(5, "shiny")`. We'll make this the implicit default in the future when `bs_theme(5, name = NULL, bootswatch = NULL, ...)` and when the theme is ready.

- We provide a `theme_bootswatch()` function that takes a `theme` argument (a theme from `bs_theme()`) and returns the name of the bootswatch theme used in the `theme`, if any. I haven't created a corresponding `theme_builtin()`, in part because it isn't strictly needed yet and in part because I find the naming of these functions slightly confusing (I initially expected `theme_bootswatch()` to return a complete bootswatch theme).


## Testing

```r
library(shiny)
# library(bslib)
pkgload::load_all()

gh_raw_base <- "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/rstudio/shiny-examples/main/081-widgets-gallery"

widget_ui <- source(file.path(gh_raw_base, "ui.R"))$value
widget_server <- source(file.path(gh_raw_base, "server.R"))$value

ui <- page_fluid(
  theme = bs_theme(name = "shiny"),
  # Make it easier to see the default input widget appearance
  tags$style(HTML(".well { background-color: unset; color: inherit;}")),
  x
)

server <- function(input, output, session) {
  widget_server(input, output)
}

shinyApp(ui, server)
```

description:
There was a small bug in #546 that would manifest when running an app via `shiny::runApp()`.

When the following app is run via `shiny::runApp()`

```r
library(shiny)
library(bslib)

ui <- fluidPage(
  navs_bar(nav("Foo", "foo"))
)

shinyApp(ui, function(...) { })
```

it will currently generate an error

```
Error in `rlang::env_name()`:

```

due to `runApp()`'s use of `eval()`. This PR catches the case of the calling function's environment being `NULL` and assumes that means the function is not being called from within Shiny. With this PR, when you exit the app, the expected deprecation warnings are printed.

You can replace `navs_bar()` with `tabsetPanel()` to verify that the deprecation warnings are appropriately muffled in `tabsetPanel()`.

```r
library(shiny)
library(bslib)

ui <- fluidPage(
  # navs_bar(nav("Foo", "foo"))
  tabsetPanel(
    tabPanel("Foo", "foo")
  )
)

shinyApp(ui, function(...) { })
```

(If testing, be sure to run via `shiny::runApp()`.)

Fixes #579

This PR improves the accessibility of the sidebar markup in three ways:

* Removes `role="main'` from the sidebar `.main` area. This is a WCAG violation, because there should only be one main landmark on the page.
* Uses `<aside>` for the sidebar, rather than `role="complimentary"`. These are functionally equivalent.
* Uses `<header>` for the sidebar title.

title: Set `role="heading"` for header of sidebar
description:
This is a minimum fix for the accessibility of the sidebar title. 

By using `role="heading"` we are effectively making the title-containing `div` look like an `h2` tag (see [implicit `aria-level`](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/Accessibility/ARIA/Roles/heading_role#associated_wai-aria_roles_states_and_properties)). 

I think it [_may_ be better to use an `h2` tag](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/Accessibility/ARIA/Roles/heading_role#best_practices) as we get predictable sizing and also more semantic HTML. While, in theory, a page could have a lot of nested sidebars, and this would be confusing, screen-readers seem to handle it fine.

title: Sidebar color CSS vars and defaults
description:
Fixes #551

## CSS Variables

The biggest part of this PR is that we now use CSS variables to set the sidebar background color. We add `--bslib-sidebar-bg` and `--bslib-sidebar-fg` by default to `.bsib-sidebar-layout`. Both `> .sidebar` and `> .collapse-toggle` will pick up their background color from these CSS variables. This means that the sidebar and toggle colors can be set with one rule applied to `.bslib-sidebar-layout`.

Internally, when `bg` or `fg` are set in `sidebar()`, we now pass that information up to `layout_sidebar()` and set those CSS variables in a `style` argument for that specific layout.

## New Background Color Default

The other change made here is to choose a default sidebar color that more closely matches the typical card-header background and that will be appropriately dark when used in a dark theme. Previously we used `$gray-100`, which looks great in the default BS theme, but for dark themes `$gray-100` is still a very light color.

The challenge here is that the card header background color is set via `$card-cap-bg` and typically defaults to an `rgba()` color (`rgba(0,0,0,0.3)` to be specific). We need an opaque color without an alpha channel for `color-contrast()` to work as expected, and also because the collapse toggle expects to obscure the sidebar border.

A mix of 3.66% results in a color blend that matches the percieved default color and works in most cases. I tested this with all of the bootswatch themes and in generally it's an improvement, although in the future we may want to patch specific themes.

title: Add ShinyResizeObserver
description:
This PR adds a layer of abstraction around our use of ResizeObservers that will unify our approach to both sidebars and cards.

## ShinyResizeObserver

It also improves our use of ResizeObservers: 

* In particular this PR ensures that contents within a sidebar resize during sidebar transition even when the sidebar appears alone on the page and not within a card.

* We now instantiate a single ResizeObserver in the client and use the same ResizeObserver to observe the main areas of any sidebar instances, rather than creating a new ResizeObserver for each sidebar instance.

* The `ShinyResizeObserver` class includes a `.flush()` method that cleans up observers on elements that are no longer present in the document. In practice, this is called whenever new sidebars are added to the page (and not on pageload), and serves as a light-weight way to ensure that we don't leak memory by keeping references to removed elements.

* A new feature of the `ShinyResizeObserver` temporarily sets `width` to `100%` for plot images during the transition. This allows the image to stretch during the transition; after the transition is complete the image is replaced by the server with a new plot image matching the final container dimensions.

* The `ShinyResizeObserver` handles contention for the same output by multiple observers. 

   In the case of nested sidebars, an output may be observed by both the outer and inner sidebars. The callback automatically keeps track of which elements have already been handled by the same callback during a resize event cycle.

   We also prevent multiple instances of `ShinyResizeObserver` from updating the same output by assigning ownership of an output to the first observer to arrive at the output. This will allow us to use separate instances of `ShinyResizeObserver` for cards and sidebars without having to worry about duplicating resize requests.

## TODO

- [x] https://github.com/rstudio/shinycoreci/pull/166
- [x] Investigate (briefly) the feasibility of only creating the ResizeObserve in a Shiny context. htmlwidgets in static documents already attach their resize method to resize events on `window`. And our RO doesn't do anything anyway unless we find a `.shiny-bound-input`, which should only happen in a Shiny context.

## Preview

### ggplot2 "static" `plotOutput()`

https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/5420529/236566433-f926813d-259d-4ca2-89af-10ee52b03ee8.mp4

title: Add `Card` class and migrate card JavaScript to TypeScript
description:
Depends on #555.
Related to #517.
Fixes #558.

This PR adds a new `Card` class that moves the card initialization JavaScript into TypeScript. I also consolidated the full screen toggle JavaScript into this class, since we were only using it via the `card()` API.

This PR also brings initialization (#555) and ResizeObserver improvements (#566) from sidebars to cards. 

Further improvements to the card component include localized event listeners, rather than relying on a global event listener. This gave us a chance to fix #558 and ensure that we expand the correct card and that we only expand one card at a time – this part is made possible in part by adding a `.bslib-has-full-screen` to the document body to prevent expanding other cards.

While in full screen, the card component will trap keyboard focus in the full screen area, ensuring that focus doesn't leak to other parts of the document body. I'll add specific tests for this case in follow-up PR in shinycoreci, but for testing you can use the app below.

<details><summary>Tab Focus App</summary>

```r
layout_column_wrap(
  width = 1 / 2,
  card(
    full_screen = TRUE,
    card_header("Nothing to focus on here"),
    shiny::p(
      "This is a boring card with just some plain text.",
      "There's something to read here but there aren't any inputs to focus on.",
      "Tabbing will only move focus to the \"Close\" button."
    )
  ),
  card(
    full_screen = TRUE,
    card_header("Inputs, oh my!"),
    shiny::p(
      "Here's a bit of text! This card does have stuff to focus on, and the",
      "first focusable element is automatically focused when the card is expanded.",
      "Try tabbing through the inputs, you can't leave!"
    ),
    shiny::selectInput("letter", "Letter", letters, selected = "a"),
    shiny::textInput("word", "Word", "hello"),
    shiny::textAreaInput("sentence", "Sentence", "hello world"),
    shiny::actionButton("go", "Go")
  ),
  card(
    full_screen = TRUE,
```

title: Improve sidebar initialization
description:
The core goal of this PR is to ensure that sidebar layouts are correctly initialized regardless of how they are loaded. There are essentially three methods of inclusion to consider:

1. A sidebar layout is present in the initial page load.
2. A sidebar layout is added to the page via `insertUI()` or `renderUI()`.
3. Both of the above.

In the final version, we use a `<script>` tag (because it's easy and available everywhere) paired with a static method `Sidebar.initCollapsibleAll()` that initializes all collapsible sidebars on the page at once.

This PR also moves from using the `Sidebar` class with only static methods as a way to collect sidebar-related functions to actually creating a `Sidebar` instance for each initialized sidebar. There are only two public methods on this class, `.isClosed` (a getter) and `.toggle()`, which accepts `"open", `"close"`, or `"toggle"` (implied when `.toggle()` is called without arguments). These are used in the `.getValue()` and `.receiveMessage()` methods of the Shiny `SidebarInputBinding`. Most of the changes in this PR are around distinguishing between static and instance methods.

Another small fix in this PR: we better coordinate the timing of the collapse toggle icon with the sidebar collapse transition itself to ensure that final state event listener fires (on the toggle icon transitionend) at the same time that the sidebar is fully collapsed.

---

Historical notes:

I tried a few ideas and have kept my exploration in tact in this PR, but the goal is the same and the approach is relatively similar:

1. If the page isn't loaded, wait for page load and then initialize all sidebar layouts.
2. Watch the DOM for new sidebar layouts and initialize them when added.

My first attempt used [mutation-summary](https://github.com/rafaelw/mutation-summary/tree/master), which is well-designed but ultimately quite heavy as a library. I then tried [arrive.js](https://www.npmjs.com/package/arrive), which is smaller and even easier to use but still a little too heavy to bundle directly into our minimized component JavaScript. The final approach in this PR is a custom class, `DocumentObserver`, built around `MutationObserver`, that does exactly what we need while building directly on browser APIs. All three versions achieve the same result, but the hand-crafted approach using `DocumentObserver` adds only about 1kB to the minified sidebar JavaScript.

While working on the dynamic UI, I reconfigured our event listeners to be better contained within the `Sidebar` class. I think this improves readability and it makes it allows us to directly attach the event listeners to targeted elements without having to rely on event bubbling. It also lets us remove unused event listeners when sidebar layouts are removed from the DOM.

It's worth pointing out that `sidebar.ts` is now just a `Sidebar` class and the `SidebarInputBinding`; the `DocumentObserver` design allows us to set up a private static object on the `Sidebar` class that handles onload and DOM observing callbacks. It also means that we only need to include the sidebar html_dependency, without needing any initialization code in the markup, and we can have a strong guarantee that any existing or new sidebars will be initialized when added to the page.

***

<details>
<summary>Test App</summary>

```r
# pak::pak("shiny@1.7.0")
# pak::pak("shiny")

library(shiny)
pkgload::load_all()
library(bslib)

INCLUDE_INITIAL_SIDEBAR <- FALSE

color_pairs <- list(
  list(dark = "#1A2A6C", light = "#AED9E0"),
  list(dark = "#800020", light = "#F6DFD7"),
  list(dark = "#4B0082", light = "#E6E6FA"),
  list(dark = "#006D5B", light = "#A2D5C6")
)

adjectives <- c("charming", "cuddly", "elegant", "fierce", "graceful", "majestic", "playful", "quirky", "silly", "witty")
animals <- c("elephant", "giraffe", "jaguar", "koala", "lemur", "otter", "panda", "panther", "penguin", "zebra")

nested_sidebar <- function(idx = 0L) {
  colors <- color_pairs[[idx %% length(color_pairs) + 1]]

  select_adjective <- function() {
    selectInput(
      paste0("adjective_", idx),
      "Adjective",
      choices = adjectives,
      selected = adjectives[idx %% length(adjectives) + 1]
    )
  }

  select_animal <- function() {
    selectInput(
      paste0("animal_", idx),
      "Animal",
      choices = animals,
      selected = animals[idx %% length(animals) + 1]
    )
  }

  layout_sidebar(
    sidebar = sidebar(
      "Outer Sidebar",
      width = 150,
      bg = colors$dark,
      select_adjective()
    ),
    height = 300,
    class = "p-0",
    fillable = TRUE,
    layout_sidebar(
      sidebar = sidebar(
        "Inner Sidebar",
        width = 150,
        bg = colors$light,
        select_animal()
      ),
      border = FALSE,
      border_radius = FALSE,
      h2("Sidebar Layout", idx),
      uiOutput(paste0("ui_content_", idx)),
    )
  ) |>
  tagAppendAttributes(class = "mb-4")
}

ui <- page_fixed(
  h1("Dynamic Sidebars"),
  tags$head(tags$title("bslib | Tests | Dynamic Sidebars")),
  p(
    "Test dynamically added sidebars.",
    "Each new layout is a nested layout with two sidebars.",
    "The sidebar collapse toggles should not overlap when collapsed",
    "and if you add the sidebar while in mobile screen width the sidebars",
    "will be closed when added."
  ),
  layout_column_wrap(
    width = 500,
    id = "sidebar-here",
    if (INCLUDE_INITIAL_SIDEBAR) nested_sidebar()
  ),
  actionButton("add_sidebar", "Add sidebar layout"),
  actionButton("remove_sidebar", "Remove sidebar layout")
)

server <- function(input, output, session) {
  idx <- 0L

  output_nested_sidebar <- function(idx) {
    output_id <- paste0("ui_content_", idx)
    adjective_id <- paste0("adjective_", idx)
    animal_id <- paste0("animal_", idx)

    output[[output_id]] <- renderUI({
      p(sprintf("Hello, %s %s!", input[[adjective_id]], input[[animal_id]]))
    })
  }

  if (INCLUDE_INITIAL_SIDEBAR) {
    observe({
      isolate(output_nested_sidebar(0))
    })
  }

  observeEvent(input$add_sidebar, {
    idx <<- idx + 1L

    insertUI(
      selector = "#sidebar-here",
      where = "beforeEnd",
      ui = nested_sidebar(idx)
    )

    output_nested_sidebar(idx)
  })

  observeEvent(input$remove_sidebar, {
    removeUI(selector = "#sidebar-here > :last-child")
  })
}

shinyApp(ui, server)
```

</details>

The above test app was used as the basis for https://github.com/rstudio/shinycoreci/pull/164

title: Implement bslib Sidebar class with static sidebar methods
description:
* Fixes #533 
* Fixes #517 

## Overview

The big objective of this PR is to introduce `BslibSidebar` a class with static methods. 

The core goal of the class is to provide a consistent method for toggling the sidebar state in `BslibSidedbar.toggleCollapse()`. This method handles finding and adding the correct classes and starting off the transition state. It pairs with the `transitionend` event listener where we set the final state of the sidebar and update the appropriate accessibility properties.

This class now also contains the initialization methods for the sidebar layout. We still have to include a small `<script>` tag in the sidebar markup, but this is now effectively just calls `<script>bslib.Sidebar.initCollapsible()</script>` on the sidebar layout that needs to be initialized.

While here I also added `sidebar_toggle()` and removed `sidebar_open()` and `sidebar_close()`. `sidebar_toggle()` takes an `open` parameter that shares the same expected values as `sidebar(open=)`, except for `"desktop"` and `NA`/`"always"` (in which case it throws an error).

## Notes

The methods re-implemented in `Sidebar` don't use jQuery. We still use jQuery for the event listeners and the Shiny input binding, but the event listeners wouldn't be hard to reimplement without jQuery. In part, the thought was to improve the portability of this class and most of what we're doing doesn't _need_ jQuery anyway.

I updated the collapse-toggle offset logic just slightly so that we're now considering only sidebar containers that are directly nested within each other. This avoids offsetting a sidebar in a card element that's contained on a navbar page with a sidebar. I've tried to think about other places where this might break expectations and have only come up with nested sidebars in tabbed card containers with a global sidebar... which I couldn't get to work right anyway.

## Example

Here's a neat example Shiny app showing off `sidebar_toggle()`.

<details>
<summary>Sidebar Toggle App</summary>

```r
library(shiny)
library(bslib)

ui <- page_navbar(
  title = "Sidebar test",
  sidebar = sidebar(
    id = "page-sidebar",
    bg = "#447098FF",
    position = "right",
    "Hello Sidebar!"
  ),
  nav(
    "Page",
    h2(
      "The sidebar is", 
      uiOutput("state", inline = TRUE, container = strong, .noWS = "after"),
      "."
    ),
    actionButton("close", "Close Sidebar"),
    actionButton("open", "Open Sidebar"),
    actionButton("toggle", "Toggle Sidebar")
  ),
  nav_spacer(),
  nav_item(
    actionLink(
      "toggle_nav",
      class = "nav-link",
      bsicons::bs_icon("list")
    )
  )
)

server <- function(input, output, session) {
  observeEvent(input$close,      sidebar_toggle("page-sidebar", open = FALSE))
  observeEvent(input$open,       sidebar_toggle("page-sidebar", open = TRUE))
  observeEvent(input$toggle,     sidebar_toggle("page-sidebar"))
  observeEvent(input$toggle_nav, sidebar_toggle("page-sidebar"))
  
  output$state <- renderUI({
    if (input[["page-sidebar"]]) "open" else "closed"
  })
}

shinyApp(ui, server)
```

</details>

title: Improve `nav_*()` and `navset_*()` function names
description:
For #476

## Overview

This is a big, wide-ranging PR with simple naming changes. There are two over-arching goals:

1. Improve the names of nav-item functions, in particular to make `nav()` more descriptive.
2. Create a better separation between `navs_` and `nav_` prefixes by replacing the first with `navset_`.

## API Changes

Here's a short summary of the changes. In all cases, deprecation warnings are emitted unless the functions are called from Shiny (to give us time to migrate the changes where `bslib::nav()` and others are called directly).

| New | Old | Shiny equiv | Notes |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| `nav_panel()` | `nav()` | `tabPanel()` |
| `nav_panel_hidden()` | `nav_content()` | `tabPanelBody()` | 1 |
| `navset_tab()` | `navs_tab()` | `tabsetPanel()` | |
| `navset_pill()` | `navs_pill()` | `tabsetPanel(type="pill")` | |
| `navset_pill_list()` | `navs_pill_list()` | `navlistPanel()` | |
| `navset_hidden()` | `navs_hidden()` | `tabSetPanel(type="hidden")` | 1 |
| `navset_bar()` | `navs_bar()` | `pageNavbar()` adjacent? | |
| `navset_card_tab()` | `navs_tab_card()` | (none) | 2 |
| `navset_card_pill()` | `navs_pill_card()` | (none) | 2 |

In the revised API, all functions starting with `navset_*()` take items prefixed with `nav_()`.

Notes:

1. `nav_content()` is now `nav_panel_hidden()` (which pairs with `navset_hidden()`). The panel itself isn't hidden necessarily; the hidden refers to the fact that there isn't a `<nav>` container with controls (e.g. a wizard interface).
2. The `_card` part of the function name was moved in front of `tab|pill` in `navset_card_tab()` and `navset_card_pill()` to reflect that card is higher priority in usage.

## PR Notes

There's a lot of work in flight in the bslib articles, so I only made changes in the R functions, documentation, and examples. We can wait for those PRs to land or we can tackle those updates in a follow-up PR.  **Update:** this is done now.

I also took care to ensure that the aliased functions appear at the end of any function lists in the documentation. All aliases are now collected in `R/navs-aliases.R` with `TODO` items so we can deprecate them in future version of bslib. **Update:** these functions will be formally deprecated.

I marked the deprecated functions as "renamed in v0.5.0". We're currently on v0.4.2.9000 and I'm assuming, from looking at our current NEWS situation that we'd be doing a minor version bump with the next release.

## Remaining work

Need to:

- [x] Clean up navset example images and ensure correct naming.
- [x] Update usage in bslib's articles.

For discussion or possibly a future PR:

- [ ] Also rename `nav_item()`? In Shiny for Python this became `nav_control()`.
- [ ] Rename `fillable` in `page_navbar()` to `fillable_panel`?

title: Restructure sidebar markup for consistency and control over color
description:
For #500 From #516 (partially) Fixes #531 ## PR Updates The main goal of this PR was to adjust the collapse toggle so that its colors match the colors of the sidebar. This uncovered a number of smaller issues that resulted in rather large changes under-the-hood. 1. Both `layout_sidebar()` and `sidebar()` gained `fg` and `bg` arguments. In both cases, if only one is provided we choose whichever of `$black` or `$white` has higher contrast for the other color. ![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/5420529/229905891-28a28822-2bf0-4bd8-89a0-af8e9578474c.png) 3. If `sidebar()` has a background color, we also set the sidebar layout container's background color. This makes the collapsing animation seamless (otherwise the sidebar disappears abruptly and we animate blank space). https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/5420529/229906145-06d0d001-4cbd-4d36-a2e0-5cb526ae83ed.mp4 5. To accommodate the last point,`sidebar()` now includes its colors in the data structure so that `layout_sidebar()` can take them into account. If they are set, the `layout_sidebar()` sets the main content area colors to match the body colors. 7. While working on the collapse toggle, I tackled #531. To ensure consistent stacking order, we now always include the sidebar elements in the following order: main, sidebar, collapse toggle. Rather than moving them in the markup, we adjust their position in the CSS. https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/5420529/229906671-894c4999-d8bd-4d06-8071-10ae0ca0c933.mp4 8. The border between main/sidebar areas is now applied to the sidebar. **Update:** with the new sidebar markup, the outer border of the layout won't receive the sidebar color. 10. While working on the border color, I also moved around our border-radius rules. The final effect is the same. 11. Lastly, after adjusting the markup and CSS, I realized that we can also move the grid column logic into the CSS. In doing this, I removed `--bslib-sidebar-columns` and `--bslib-sidebar-columns-collapsed` and replaced them with a `--bslib-sidebar-width` CSS variable. I also ensured that the sidebar is never wider than the parent container. The end result is that everything we set in the attributes or CSS of the sidebar layout relate to state or user preference. 12. The collapse toggle buttons now maintain their position through all states on mobile. This is consistent with sidebar toggles on desktop. In other words, the second-level sidebar is always second from the right on mobile. 14. The sidebar now defaults to `$gray-100`. This default is set via the `$bslib-sidebar-bg` SASS variable, which could be set at the theme level, in addition to `$bslib-sidebar-fg`. The sidebar background and foreground are still locally configurable via the `bg` and `fg` arguments described at the top of this PR. ![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/5420529/231275902-565aef2f-6692-4b5f-9b4d-b5b7db1d5281.png) ## Examples Among other examples, I've been using the code below to generate many card variations for testing and review.
Example ```r library(bslib) colors <- list( list(color = "#FFFAFA", name = "Snow"), list(color = "#B22222", name = "Fire Brick"), list(color = "#2F4F4F", name = "Dark Slate Gray"), list(color = "#556B2F", name = "Dark Olive Green"), list(color = "#483D8B", name = "Dark Slate Blue"), list(color = "#00FA9A", name = "Medium Spring Green"), list(color = "#8B4513", name = "Saddle Brown"), list(color = "#FFDAB9", name = "Peach Puff"), list(color = "#228B22", name = "Forest Green"), list(color = "#FFD700", name = "Gold"), list(color = "#8B008B", name = "Dark Magenta"), list(color = "#FF8C00", name = "Dark Orange"), list(color = "#FF69B4", name = "Hot Pink"), list(color = "#4169E1", name = "Royal Blue"), list(color = "#00CED1", name = "Dark Turquoise"), list(color = "#F0E68C", name = "Khaki") ) sidebars <- lapply(colors, function(x) { do_main_bg <- runif(1) > 0.5 do_border <- runif(1) > 0.5 do_border_radius <- runif(1) > 0.5 do_border_color <- FALSE # runif(1) > 0.75 sb_width <- paste0(floor(runif(1, 150, 500)), "px") sb_pos <- sample(c("left", "right"), 1) as_card <- runif(1) > 0.5 state <- sample(c(TRUE, FALSE, NA), 1) ret <- layout_sidebar( sidebar = sidebar( position = sb_pos, width = sb_width, open = state, bg = if (prismatic::clr_extract_lightness(x$color) > 50) { as.character(prismatic::clr_darken(x$color, 0.1)) } else { as.character(prismatic::clr_lighten(x$color, 0.1)) }, HTML(sprintf( "Sidebar: %s
position: %s
border: %s
radius: %s
width: %s
open: %s", x$name, sb_pos, do_border, do_border_radius, sb_width, if (is.na(state)) "always" else if (state) "open" else "closed" )) ), height = "350px", bg = if (do_main_bg) x$color, border = do_border, border_radius = do_border_radius, border_color = if (do_border_color) "#00CED1", lorem::ipsum(1, 2) ) if (!as_card) htmltools::tagAppendAttributes(ret, class = "my-2") else { card( class = "my-2", if (runif(1) > 0.25) card_header("A Card"), ret ) } }) extra_sidebars <- list( layout_sidebar( height = "300px", sidebar = sidebar("Default sidebar"), p("Default content"), lorem::ipsum(1, 2) ), layout_sidebar( sidebar( width = "33%", fg = "#9B59B6", p("width: 33%") ), lorem::ipsum(1, 2) ), layout_sidebar( fillable = TRUE, class = "p-0", sidebar( width = "20%", bg = "#FF7847", fg = "", "Left Sidebar 1" ), layout_sidebar( fillable = TRUE, class = "p-0", border = FALSE, border_radius = FALSE, sidebar( width = "30%", bg = "#FF70A6", position = "right", "Right Sidebar" ), layout_sidebar( border = FALSE, border_radius = FALSE, sidebar( width = "40%", bg = "#FFB499", "Left Sidebar 2", ), lorem::ipsum(3, 1) ) ) ) ) page_fluid( layout_column_wrap( width = "400px", fill = TRUE, !!!extra_sidebars, !!!sidebars ) ) page_fixed( div( class = "my-5", !!!extra_sidebars, !!!sidebars ) ) ```

title: Improve/expand sidebar initial open state options
description:
For #500
From #516

The primary goal of this PR is to introduce a new sidebar initial state option, where the sidebar is open on desktop screens and closed on mobile on load. To make room for this option, `open` now accepts `"desktop"` (the new default), `"open"`, `"closed"` or `"always"`. The last three correspond to the previous values of `TRUE`, `FALSE`, and `NA`, and the elder values will continue to work as expected.

The intial state determined on load works as follows:

1. The sidebar markup is initially written as if the sidebar will be open, but will have an additional `data-sidebar-init-auto-collapse="true"` attribute on the layout element.
2. In the CSS, within the media queries for `sm` down, we set a CSS variable `--bslib-sidebar-js-init-collapsed: true` for elements with this attribute. This CSS variable is only true if the window is at or below the `sm` breakpoint.
3. During initalization, if we encounter an element with the signalling data attribute, we query the value of the CSS variable for the element. If the CSS variable is set and equal to `"true"`, we're on a small screen and can collapse the sidebar. We then add the appropriate class and adjust the `aria-expanded` property on the collapsed toggle.

Note that intial decision to have the sidebar initially open or closed only happen on page load. If a viewer starts with a very small window that they expand to desktop sizes, the sidebars won't expand until they open them (or if they reload the page).

Along the way, I realized we could simplify some of the logic and not include the collapse toggle if `open = "always"`. I also added tests around the interaction between `open`, `id`, and the aria attributes on the collapse toggle.

title: Add `max_height_mobile` to `sidebar()`
description:
For #500
From #516

Adds `max_height_mobile` argument to `sidebar()`. The max height is enforced by the `grid-template-rows` property of the sidebar layout on small screens, where we wrap the users' value in `fit-content()`, which ensures that the sidebar's row follows the content height, limiting it to our desired maximum value.

The default is `fit-content(250px)` in general or `fit-content(50%)` when `layout_sidebar()` has a specified `height`. These defaults are applied when `max_height_mobile = NULL` because we need to determine the default value inside `layout_sidebar()` when we know whether or not the layout has a fixed height. This does point out that relative units won't work unless the layout has an opinionated height.

## Examples

| Natural Height | Fixed Height |
|:---:|:---:|
| ![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/5420529/229220027-5e29ce83-bd4f-4070-aaa9-e85e178e30ec.png) | ![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/5420529/229220113-f3245b4e-53e3-437e-af74-3d383f49a44b.png) |

<details>
<summary>Example</summary>

```r
# sidebar/max-height-mobile
pkgload::load_all()

lorem_1 <- lorem::ipsum(1, 2)
lorem_2 <- lorem::ipsum(2, 2)

page_fixed(
  h2("Generic sidebar layout"),
  p("Mobile sidebar takes up 250px by default."),
  layout_sidebar(
    sidebar(lorem_2),
    lorem_1
  ),
  h2("Generic sidebar layout, custom max height"),
  p(code('max_height_mobile = "150px"')),
  layout_sidebar(
    sidebar(lorem_2, max_height_mobile = "150px"),
    lorem_1
  ),
  h2("Fixed height layout"),
  p("Mobile sidebar takes up 50% by default."),
  layout_sidebar(
    sidebar(lorem_2),
    height = "300px",
    lorem_1
  ),
  h2("Fixed height layout, custom max height"),
  p(code('max_height_mobile = "66%"')),
  layout_sidebar(
    sidebar(lorem_2, max_height_mobile = "66%"),
    height = "300px",
    lorem_1
  ),
  br(),
  br()
)
```

</details>

title: Sidebar: `border` and `border_radius` default to `NULL`
description:
For #500
From #516

When explicitly enabled via `border = TRUE` or `border_radius = TRUE`, a data attribute is added to the `.bslib-sidebar-layout` container indicating the user intent: `data-bslib-sidebar-border="true"` and `data-bslib-sidebar-border-radius="true"`. Conversely, if disabled, the data attribute value is `"false"`. This lets other components include rules to enabled or disable the sidebar borders and border radius in the default case while taking into account the user intent, thereby allowing the user to force borders in places where our layouts would otherwise include or hide them.

title: Add `title` argument to `sidebar()`
description:
For #500

Adds a `title` argument to `sidebar()`. If a bare character or numeric, the `title` is wrapped in a `div` with class `sidebar-title`, which sets the font size, line-height, margin, padding and adds a bottom border to the title. Alternatively, users can provide their own tag (and manually apply the `sidebar-title` class as needed).

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/5420529/229160178-444854a0-2a9c-414b-8449-4fd2172c5314.png)

The CSS rule for the sidebar title is `.bslib-sidebar-layout .sidebar-title` (i.e. the rule doesn't include the `.sidebar` class) to ensure the lowest possible specificity. Even then, one potentially surprising thing is that when using a heading element, like `h3()`, our font size rule will have higher specificity. Users who want to adjust the font-size of the sidebar title should use the `.fs-{1-6}` utility classes instead (and probably shouldn't use a heading element).

```r
layout_sidebar(
  sidebar(
    bg = "#F1F3F5",
    title = div("Shine On", class = "sidebar-title fs-2"),
    "Sidebar filters, etc..."
  ),
  "Main content area"
)
```

The sidebar title works well with accordions, where the margins will be adjusted and the bottom border is removed (if `:has()` is supported) or hidden via positioning.

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/5420529/229160602-24c78961-bc83-421d-9e8b-585bc61d0275.png)


While workign on this, I also realized that we should similarly adjust margins and borders when the accordion is *not* the first or last item in the sidebar. When there is content preceeding the accordion, we retain the `margin-top` on the accordion container and the `border-top` of the first accordion item; similarly if there is content after the accordion, we do the same for the bottom margin and border.

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/5420529/229162760-df377dfb-a7e0-4f5d-a852-ae49febdd3d1.png)

title: Improve sidebar transition and collapsed state
description:
Fixes #518

* The collapsed sidebar now has `height: 0` so that it doesn't affec the size of the sidebar layout when collapsed.
* While transitioning, we now maintain `height`, `width`, and `padding` of `0`. This avoids jarring layout shifts as the sidebar expands. It's also makes the expanding and collapsing transitions symmetric (previously the sidebar would dissappear immediately when collapsing but be revealed immediately while expanding).

## Before

In the original behavior, if the sidebar contained a text node (rather than an element node), the collapsed sidebar would have a fairly large height, caused be the unseen text wrapping in the `width: 0` sidebar container.

https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/5420529/229144510-5fe8478e-d13d-4f41-926e-ab10c3e05534.mp4


## Collapsed height 0

This is fixed by setting `height: 0` of the sidebar in the collapsed state. Which resolves the starting and end states of the transition in either direction. But notice that when expanding, the sidebar is revealed immediately and as its width grows to the final state the content within shifts considerably.

https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/5420529/229144747-9972be27-5028-4c3f-a37d-e20342a85e9b.mp4

It's even more pronounced with additional content in the sidebar.

https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/5420529/229142775-929bf948-5bec-4858-835d-fade96fead94.mp4

## Now

By setting keeping the sidebar's collapsed state of `height: 0; width: 0; padding: 0` until `.transitioning` is removed, we can minimize the layout shift that occurs when the sidebar appears.

https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/5420529/229142030-88791469-ef57-46a8-9bac-aa0243b57db0.mp4


## Testing

Here is a simple UI I used for testing the animations in various settings.

<details>
<summary>Testing</summary>

```r
pkgload::load_all()

card_all_small <-
  card(
    card_header("Card with sidebar"),
    layout_sidebar(
      sidebar = sidebar("Card Sidebar", open = FALSE),
      "My card"
    ),
    card_footer("footer of said card")
  )

card_long_main <-
  card(
    card_header("Card with sidebar"),
    layout_sidebar(
      sidebar = sidebar("Card Sidebar", open = FALSE),
      lorem::ipsum(4, 1)
    ),
    card_footer("footer of said card")
  )

card_long_sidebar <-
  card(
    card_header("Card with sidebar"),
    layout_sidebar(
      sidebar = sidebar(
        lorem::ipsum(4, 1),
        open = FALSE
      ),
      "My card"
    ),
    card_footer("footer of said card")
  )

card_fixed_height <-
  card(
    height = "300px",
    card_header("Fixed height card with long sidebar"),
    layout_sidebar(
      sidebar = sidebar(
        lorem::ipsum(4, 1),
        open = FALSE
      ),
      "My card"
    ),
    card_footer("footer of said card")
  )

page_fixed(
  div(
    class = "m-4",
    h2("Short sidebar"),
    card_all_small,
    h2("Short sidebar, long card"),
    card_long_main,
    h2("Long sidebar, short content"),
    card_long_sidebar,
    h2("Fixed height card"),
    card_fixed_height,
    h2("Cards in a layout"),
    layout_column_wrap(
      width = "500px",
      fixed_width = FALSE,
      heights_equal = "row",
      card_all_small,
      card_fixed_height,
      card_long_main,
      card_long_sidebar
    )
  )
)
```

</details>

title: Improve examples in `navs_tab()` and family
description:
Updates the examples for `navs_tab()`, `navs_pill()`, etc. to include complete and (nearly) selc-contained examples that are more friendly for copy-pasting.

I tried unsuccessfully to come up with a solution that uses the `@examples` section combined with a [custom `pkgdown_print` method](https://pkgdown.r-lib.org/reference/pkgdown_print.html).  Unfortunately there are a few too many moving pieces for that approach to work right now.

The approach in this PR is to use an Rmd fragment (aka child document in a roxygen2 context) that renders the examples, takes a screenshot, and then replaces the output with the screenshot. The previews are static as a result, but they also appear in both the pkgdown site and the R package docs, which is overall an improvement in my opinion.

By default the screenshot previews are re-generated when calling `devtools::document()` on CI so they will automatically stay up to date with our routine workflows. I've also modified bslib's `routine.sh` to run `optipng` on png files in `man/figures` to keep the images small. In the end, they're each about 10 KB or less.

title: Sidebar improvements
description: This PR covers the improvements listed in #500 (checkmarks indicate if the item has been moved to an individual PR) 1. [x] `sidebar()` gains a `title` argument that is wrapped in ``. The font sizes and formatting try to balance all of the places where sidebars can appear. Users can also pass a tag element that is added directly to the top of the sidebar (they may want to include the `sidebar-title` class when they do). 2. [x] I adjusted the styles for accordions inside sidebars to ensure we keep the top or bottom border of `.accordion` elements that aren't the first or last child, respectively. This also helps the sidebar title fit into sidebars with accordions. 3. [x] The `open` argument of `sidebar()` is now a single-choice argument with options `"desktop"`, `"open"`, `"closed"`, and `"always"`. We still accept `TRUE`, `FALSE` and `NA` for the last three. The new default, `"desktop"`, causes the sidebar to be collapsed initially on mobile devices. The sidebar state is determined based on the viewport width on initialization, i.e. we don't watch the viewport for changes. When `open = "desktop"`, we add a `data-sidebar-init-auto-collapse="true"` attribute to the sidebar layout element. Then, during initialization, we use this attribute as a signal to decide the sidebar state for this element. Separately, we use a CSS rule wrapped in a media query that sets `--bslib-sidebar-js-init-collapsed: true` for elements with the signaling attribute. During initialization, we can check this variable and rely on the fact that the browser will have computed the style for the sidebar and knows whether we're in the smaller screen size. Also: I initially used `md` as the breakpoint, rather than `sm` (which is where sidebars move to the top). While `md` felt like the right point to me, it also opens up the door to too many other possibilities. With `sm` the hidden/collapsed behavior is aligned with the mobile layout. 5. [x] `sidebar()` gains a `max_height_mobile` argument, which should be a valid CSS unit. When not provided, the default will be `250px`, unless the `layout_sidebar()` where the sidebar appears has a defined `height`, in which case we'll set it to `50%`. The max height is enforced via `fit-content()` in the `grid-template-rows` property for sidebar layouts on mobile. When applied, the grid row holding the sidebar should match the natural height of the sidebar until reaching the upper limit, at which point the sidebar contents will scroll. 6. [x] The `border` and `border_radius` arguments of `layout_sidebar()` now default to `NULL`. When non-null, an additional class is added in the form `.sidebar-{border,border-radius}-{enabled,disabled}` to carry the user intent. Our default styling rules, e.g. in cards, then turn off border and border radius, conditioned on `:not(.sidebar-border-enabled)` and `:not(.sidebar-border-radius-enabled)`, respectively. 7. [x] While working on the last point, I realized that the sidebar collapse toggle becomes invisible on dark backgrounds. I updated the `background-color` of the collapse toggle to slightly transparent white, ensuring the toggle is visible on all backgrounds while inheriting the main content area colors. This required slightly adjusting the position of the toggle button so that it doesn't overlap with the sidebar border. | Before | After | |:--:|:--:| | | |

title: (Re)-Introducing card(), value_box(), and layout_column_wrap()
description:
This PR is a follow up to #452, which added new `card()` API as well as `value_box()` and `layout_column_wrap()`. To learn more about this new functionality, refer to these new pkgdown articles

* https://rstudio.github.io/bslib/articles/cards.html 
* https://rstudio.github.io/bslib/articles/value-boxes.html 
* https://rstudio.github.io/bslib/articles/layouts.html 

This PR updates how [responsive sizing](https://rstudio.github.io/bslib/articles/cards.html#responsive-sizing) (i.e., `card_body_fill()`) works by using the new `bindFillRole()` function in `{htmltools}`. Note that `shiny::plotOutput()` and `htmlwidgets::shinyWidgetOutput()` will also make use of this to make plots and widgets fill by default when they are a direct child of `card_body_fill()`:

https://github.com/rstudio/htmltools/pull/345
https://github.com/rstudio/shiny/pull/3715
https://github.com/ramnathv/htmlwidgets/pull/442

### Testing notes

Automated tests are being added in https://github.com/rstudio/shinycoreci/pull/132


It'd be great to have the same/similar tests running against our pro products and manually tested on Firefox, Safari, and Edge (see the tests added in https://github.com/rstudio/shinycoreci/pull/132 for expected behavior).

https://github.com/rstudio/bslib/tree/main/inst/examples/card
https://github.com/rstudio/bslib/tree/main/inst/examples/value_box

Also, when testing these, make sure to install the development version of `{bslib}` this way (which will also install the development version of some other packages):

```r
remotes::install_github("rstudio/bslib")
```

title: Revert to pre-Bootstrap 5 nav bs3compat shimming
description:
In #304, I changed the overall approach to shimming Bootstrap's `$.fn.tab` jQuery plugin (I wanted to move away from assuming that it exists), but that approach won't work when tabs are shown programmatically (e.g., `shinycoreci-apps/apps/213-tab-panels`). 

This reverts it to use the same `.noConflict()` approach we were using before in a way that works for Bootstrap 5. Originally, I thought that this approach wasn't going to work at all because Bootstrap 5 doesn't register this plugin until the DOM is ready, but now that we execute this code after the DOM is ready, this approach seems to work fine.

title: Add navs_tab_card() and navs_pill_card()
description: Adds `navs_tab_card()` and `navs_pill_card()`, which are similar to `navs_tab()` and `navs_pill()`, but they wrap the nav items in a card header and the content in the card body. As a result, these new nav containers provide an effective way to add padding and borders around the nav content, making it appear less like content is floating in space (compare these examples to the ones in https://github.com/rstudio/bslib/pull/319): ```r library(shiny) nav_items <- list( nav("a", "tab a"), nav("b", "tab b"), nav_item( tags$a(icon("github"), "Shiny", href = "https://github.com/rstudio/shiny", target = "_blank") ), nav_spacer(), nav_menu( "Other links", align = "right", nav("c", "tab c"), nav_item( tags$a(icon("r-project"), "RStudio", href = "https://rstudio.com", target = "_blank") ) ) ) navs_tab_card(!!!nav_items) ``` ```r navs_pill_card(!!!nav_items) ```

title: Add nav_item() and nav_spacer() for external links, inline forms, and alignment
description: This PR adds 2 new convenience functions for the new `nav()` API: * `nav_item()`: for placing links, buttons, and inline forms within `navs_tab()`, `navs_bar()`, etc. * `nav_spacer()`: for adding space between navigation items (useful for creating right aligned `nav_item()`) It also adds an align argument to `nav_menu()` for aligning the dropdown menu (useful now that it's easy to right-align navigation items): ```r library(shiny) library(bslib) nav_items <- list( nav("a", "tab a"), nav("b", "tab b"), nav_item( tags$a(icon("github"), "Shiny", href = "https://github.com/rstudio/shiny", target = "_blank") ), nav_spacer(), nav_menu( "Other links", align = "right", nav("c", "tab c"), nav_item( tags$a(icon("r-project"), "RStudio", href = "https://rstudio.com", target = "_blank") ) ) ) shinyApp( page_navbar( title = "Title", bg = "#0062cc", !!!nav_items ), function(...) { } ) ``` Also works with `navs_pill()`: ```r shinyApp( navs_pill(!!!nav_items), function(...) { } ) ``` And `navs_pill_list()` (in this context, `nav_spacer()` functions as a vertical spacer): ```r shinyApp( page_fluid( tags$head(tags$style(".tab-content * {height: 100vh}")), navs_pill_list(!!!nav_items) ), function(...) { } ) ```

title: New nav() api providing legacy support for shiny's tabPanel() logic
description: (To be merged after https://github.com/rstudio/htmltools/pull/224) This PR moves essentially all of the server-side logic behind `{shiny}`'s `tabPanel()` logic and exports it via a new API (in future PRs, we'll be expanding on this new API to provide new functionality). Here's a map from the old API to the new one: ### Creating navs * `nav()` (i.e., `tabPanel()`) * `nav_menu()` (i.e., `navbarMenu()`) * `navs_tab()` (i.e., `tabsetPanel(type = "tabs")`) * `navs_pill()` (i.e., `tabsetPanel(type = "pill")`) * `navs_hidden()` (i.e., `tabsetPanel(type = "hidden")`) * `navs_pill_list()` (i.e., `navlistPanel()`) * `navs_bar()` (i.e., `navbarPage()`) Note that the `navs_*()` consumer functions (e.g., `navs_tab()`) generate a result that prints a static HTML page ```r tabs <- navs_tab( nav("a", "a"), nav("b", "b") ) tabs ``` But you can also put them inside new page constructor functions that default `theme` to `bs_theme()` (the latest recommended version of Bootstrap). ```r page_fluid(tabs) ``` ### Updating navs * `nav_select()` (i.e., `updateTabsetPanel()`) * `nav_insert()` (i.e., `insertTab()`) * `nav_prepend()` (i.e., `prependTab()`) * `nav_append()` (i.e., `appendTab()`) * `nav_remove()` (i.e., `removeTab()`) * `nav_show()` (i.e., `showTab()`) * `nav_hide()` (i.e., `hideTab()`)

title: Emit warning when bs_global_set() is called inside runtime: shiny
description:
And recommend using `session$setCurrentTheme()` instead. The intention is to avoid confusion when trying to do something like:

````
---
runtime: shiny
output: 
  html_document:
    theme:
      version: 4
---

```{r}
bslib::bs_global_theme_update(bg = "black", fg = "white", primary = "purple")
```

```{r}
# One might expect the slider to be purple, not blue
sliderInput("foo", "bar", 1, 3, 2)
```
````


Which works as expected without `runtime: shiny`, but inside of a shiny runtime, the more proper way to do this is to do this instead

````
---
runtime: shiny
output: 
  html_document:
    theme:
      version: 4
---

```{r, include=FALSE}
session$setCurrentTheme(bslib::bs_theme(bg = "black", fg = "white", primary = "purple"))
```

```{r}
# One might expect the slider to be purple, not blue
sliderInput("foo", "bar", 1, 3, 2)
```
````

title: Use `tools::R_user_dir()` when possible
description:
This PR addresses this comment from CRAN:


```
Also, checking creates and leaves behind
   ~/.cache/R-bslib

in violation of the CRAN Policy's

   Packages should not write in the user's home filespace (including
   clipboards), nor anywhere else on the file system apart from the R
   session's temporary directory (or during installation in the location
   pointed to by TMPDIR: and such usage should be cleaned up). Installing
   into the system's R installation (e.g., scripts to its bin directory)
   is not allowed.

   Limited exceptions may be allowed in interactive sessions if the
   package obtains confirmation from the user.

   For R version 4.0 or later (hence a version dependency is required or
   only conditional use is possible), packages may store user-specific
   data, configuration and cache files in their respective user
   directories obtained from tools::R_user_dir(), provided that by
   default sizes are kept as small as possible and the contents are
   actively managed (including removing outdated material).

Can you please change as necessary, ideally using the
tools::R_user_dir() mechanism where available?
```

When re-submitting to CRAN, it would be a good idea to mention that the behavior is fixed on R 4.0, but unchanged for older versions of R.

title: Fixes and changes to bootstrap accessibility plugin
description:
https://github.com/paypal/bootstrap-accessibility-plugin has several issues:

(1) [It assumes that the page is already loaded before it runs](https://github.com/paypal/bootstrap-accessibility-plugin/blob/fbbf870eafc1ee5d4547fabbeea71778ddbe2166/src/js/tab.js#L4-L12), so the aria labels aren't added on page load to something like this:

```{r}
library(shiny)
ui <- fluidPage(
  theme = bslib::bs_theme(version = 3),
  tabsetPanel(
    tabPanel("A", "a"),
    tabPanel("B", "b")
  )
)
server <- function(input, output) {}
shinyApp(ui, server)
```

(2) It always provides outlines for mouse interactions, which is quite a deviation in visual style, and probably annoying most users, so we've made these mouse outlines an opt-in feature via a Sass variable called `$mouse-outline-style`:

```r
library(shiny)
ui <- fluidPage(
  theme = bslib::bs_theme(version = 3, "mouse-outline-style" = "auto"),
  tabsetPanel(
    tabPanel("A", "a"),
    tabPanel("B", "b")
  )
)
server <- function(input, output) {}
shinyApp(ui, server)
```

(3) As a consequence of opt-ing out of mouse-based outlines, keyboard navigation suffers on Chrome, so we've decided to enable `:focus-visible` outlines by default, so keyboard navigation is supported on browsers that support it.

```r
library(shiny)
ui <- fluidPage(
  theme = bslib::bs_theme(version = 3, "keyboard-outline-color" = "red"),
  tabsetPanel(
    tabPanel("A", "a"),
    tabPanel("B", "b")
  )
)
server <- function(input, output) {}
shinyApp(ui, server)
```

```r
theme <- bs_theme_get()
```

On the other hand, if the app's source is copy/pasted into the R console, then the bootstraplib theme will always be cleared after the app exits:

title: Use consistent output directory for bootstrap()
description:
This PR does the following:

* When the inputs are the same, it uses the same output directory every time. If the output directory already exists, it won't bother writing files there.
* Adds a wrapper function `system_file()`, which is faster than `system.file`. (The latter was a bottleneck.)

Before the `system_file` change:
```
> system.time(bootstrap())
   user  system elapsed 
  0.403   0.038   0.441 
> system.time(bootstrap())
   user  system elapsed 
  0.034   0.009   0.043
```

After:

```
> system.time(bootstrap())
   user  system elapsed 
  0.385   0.032   0.416 
> system.time(bootstrap())
   user  system elapsed 
  0.010   0.003   0.013 
```

This should be merged after https://github.com/rstudio/sass/pull/44. (The `Remotes` field here will have to be updated after that PR is merged.)


*****

Testing notes:

Run the following. Each time you run `dir(outdir)`, the output should be the same -- there should be exactly one directory listed with a name like `"bootstrap-xxxxxxx"`. If there is more than one such directory, then there's a problem.

```R
library(bootstraplib)
outdir <- file.path(tempdir(), "bootstraplib")

bootstrap()
dir(outdir)
#> [1] "bootstrap-560e344a81bc5cbe"

bootstrap()
dir(outdir)
#> [1] "bootstrap-560e344a81bc5cbe"
```

```r
        on line 1:19 of stdin
>> $font-family-base: * !default;
```

title: bs_theme_quick feature
description:
## Goal

Allow users to specify a _very_ small number of colors and have the entire theme change to reflect that. Currently the only required colors are `bg` and `fg`, with optional `accent` (primary) and `secondary` colors.

## Example

```r
bs_theme_quick(bg = "black", fg = "white", accent = "red")
```

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/129551/74959882-38cce600-53c0-11ea-8556-993c5cb381f6.png)

## Limitations

- **`dark` and `light` lose their intuitive meanings.** If you specify a dark bg and light fg, then `dark` and `light` mean "closer to bg" and "closer to fg", not luminosity.

## TODO

- [x] Implement bs3 version
- [x] Unit tests
- [x] Remove dependency on `shiny:::parseCssColor` (move to htmltools?)

## Open questions

- Should the function actually add the theme, or just generate it? **The exported bs_theme_quick function actually adds it; the underlying (un-exported) functions bs4_theme_quick and bs3_theme_quick just generate.**
- Add fonts? (Seems like the next most common thing that will come up) We could do just one font, or separate fonts for body, heading, buttons/inputs...  **Not as part of this function**

feat(navs): Use the navset id as the tabset id
description:
## Summary

When a navset has a user-supplied `id=`, use it as the `data-tabsetid` (and in the derived `tab-<tabsetid>-<index>` pane ids) instead of minting a random integer.

**Before:** `data-tabsetid="4785"` / `id="tab-4785-1"`
**After:** `data-tabsetid="my_tabs"` / `id="tab-my_tabs-1"`

This makes the rendered markup reproducible across renders and straightforward to target from custom CSS and JavaScript.

This is the R counterpart of posit-dev/py-shiny#2410, which makes the same change in Shiny for Python. `buildTabset()` is the single place tabset ids are minted — `shiny::tabsetPanel()`, `navbarPage()`, `navlistPanel()` and `tabPanel()` all delegate here, so no change is needed in rstudio/shiny.

## The selector-safety caveat

py-shiny gets this for free because `validate_id()` restricts input ids to `^\.?\w+$`. **R has no equivalent** — `shiny::NS()` just pastes, and there's no validation on the leaf id. So `tabsetPanel(id = "my.tabs")` is legal R today, and naively reusing it would emit `href="#tab-my.tabs-1"`, which a browser parses as `#tab-my` + `.tabs-1` → tab switching silently breaks.

So the id is only reused when it matches `^[A-Za-z0-9_-]+$` (`-` included because that's `ns.sep`). Anything else falls back to the random integer, i.e. to exactly today's behavior. Anonymous navsets and `nav_menu()` dropdowns keep the random id as before.

## Changes

- **`R/navs-legacy.R`** New internal `tabset_id()` helper; `buildTabset()` calls it instead of `p_randomInt()` directly.
- **`tests/testthat/test-navs-legacy.R`** Tests for `tabset_id()` and for the rendered markup: id reuse, stability across renders, module-style `mod-tabs` ids, the anonymous fallback, `nav_menu()` keeping its own id, and the unsafe-id fallback.
- **`NEWS.md`** Entry under a new Improvements section.

## Verification

- Full suite: **1152 passing**, no snapshot changes (no existing bslib snapshot contains `data-tabsetid`). The 2 failures in `test-rmd-skeletons.R` are a local environment gap — `thematic` isn't installed — and are unrelated.
- Confirmed the new tests are load-bearing: reverting `buildTabset()` to `p_randomInt()` fails 6 of them.
